subject: microbiology
title: History of Microbiology: Koch Postulates, Pasteur, Lister and Leeuwenhoek

steps.tx: **Koch postulates** demand four proofs before a microbe is blamed for a disease: the organism occurs in every case, it is isolated in pure culture, the culture reproduces disease in a healthy host, and it is re-isolated from that host. Robert Koch built them on anthrax, tuberculosis and cholera work, and they remain the logic skeleton beneath modern causal claims even where viruses, uncultivable organisms and carrier states force their molecular revision.
steps.say: Find it, grow it, reproduce it, recover it: Koch's four proofs still frame causal claims.

nodes.label: Organism in every case of disease
Culture causes disease in healthy host

steps.tx: **Antonie van Leeuwenhoek**, a draper grinding single lenses in Delft, first saw bacteria and protozoa in 1670s letters to the Royal Society, calling them animalcules in water, dental plaque and his own stool. His microscopes magnified about 270 fold with a single bead lens, better than compound instruments of his century, and microbiology begins with his curiosity rather than any theory of disease.
steps.say: A draper's bead lens saw bacteria a century before anyone knew what they did.

left.title: Leeuwenhoek's world
points: Letters to the Royal Society as publications
No disease theory attached to his microbes

right.title: What followed
points: Germ theory awaited Pasteur and Koch
Morphology first: cocci, bacilli, spirilla named
Leeuwenhoek commemorated as father of microbiology

steps.tx: **Louis Pasteur** refuted spontaneous generation with swan neck flasks (broth stays sterile until dust enters), proved microbes cause fermentation and silkworm disease, and converted germ theory into vaccines: attenuated chicken cholera, anthrax at Pouilly le Fort, and rabies post exposure treatment in 1885. Pasteurisation and the Pasteur Institute complete a career that founded microbiology as an experimental science and immunology as its application.
steps.say: Pasteur killed spontaneous generation with a bent glass neck and built vaccines from attenuation.

left.title: Pasteur's proofs
points: Swan neck flasks refute spontaneous generation
Fermentation is microbial, not purely chemical
Germ theory of disease experimentally grounded

right.title: Pasteur's vaccines
points: Pasteurisation from wine and milk work

steps.tx: **Joseph Lister**, reading Pasteur, sprayed carbolic acid over surgical wounds and instruments in 1867 and watched compound fracture and amputation mortality fall, founding antiseptic surgery. Semmelweis's earlier handwashing data (chlorinated lime, puerperal fever) and Nightingale's sanitation statistics complete the pre antibiotic infection control triad that modern sterile technique inherited and converted from antisepsis to asepsis.
steps.say: Lister sprayed carbolic acid and surgical sepsis fell; asepsis is his idea matured.

left.title: Antisepsis era
points: Antiseptics kill microbes in and around wounds
Mortality falls documented ward by ward

right.title: Asepsis succession
points: Exclude microbes rather than kill in situ

steps.tx: **Koch's laboratory technology** made the postulates executable: solid media (agar suggested by Fanny Hesse, replacing gelatin that melted and was eaten), the Petri dish from his assistant, aniline dyes and the Gram and acid fast stains, and pure culture technique. His 1882 tuberculosis announcement and 1883 cholera expedition are dated by these tools as much as by genius, a recurring history lesson that methods precede discoveries.
steps.say: Agar, Petri dishes and dyes came before the famous identifications; methods precede discoveries.

left.title: Koch's toolkit
points: Petri dish and streak plate pure cultures

right.title: Koch's identifications
points: Cholera vibrio in Egypt and India (1883)

steps.tx: The **postulates fail instructively** where biology disobeys them: viruses uncultivable in Koch's media ( Rivers postulates later), asymptomatic carriers (Typhoid Mary sheds Salmonella Typhi healthily), uncultivable organisms (Treponema pallidum, Mycobacterium leprae for decades), polymicrobial diseases, and organisms that cause disease only in compromised hosts. Molecular Koch postulates (Falkow) relocate proof to virulence genes: delete it, lose disease; restore it, regain it.
steps.say: Carriers, viruses and uncultivable organisms broke the postulates; genes inherited their logic.

left.title: Classical failures
points: Leprae and pallidum resist routine culture
Opportunists need host defects to harm

right.title: Modern revisions
points: Molecular postulates: virulence gene deletion and restoration
Animal models and organoids substitute hosts

steps.tx: The **golden age cascade** (1876 to 1910) named a pathogen per year at its peak: Neisser's gonococcus, Loeffler's diphtheria bacillus, Klebs's and, in the usual telling, the roster examiners sample from history questions beside their organisms. Each identification converted a clinical syndrome into a transmissible agent with a culture, a stain and eventually a therapy, which is why historical pairings (Koch TB, Pasteur rabies, Lister antisepsis) remain shorthand.
steps.say: A microbe a year for three decades turned syndromes into agents with stains and cultures.

right.title: Supporting cast
points: Petri and Hesse: dish and agar
Ehrlich: acid fast stain roots, chemotherapy
Fleming, Florey, Chain: penicillin era opening

steps.tx: **History questions test** one discipline beyond dates: separating observation, mechanism and application. Leeuwenhoek observed without mechanism, Pasteur mechanised without seeing most agents, Koch proved causation with new methods, Lister applied before proof was complete. Examiners reward candidates who place each name at the right station of that sequence rather than in a single inventor blur.
steps.say: Observation, mechanism, proof, application: place each name at its station.
